evidence.quote: Does the condition 1/pn < ∞ for positive integers pn guarantee that p the sequences of powers {z } fails to span C(γ) for every Jordan arc γ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{p_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of positive integers satisfying
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{p_n}<\infty.$$
For a Jordan arc $\gamma\subset\mathbb{C}$, let $C(\gamma)$ denote the Banach space of continuous complex-valued functions on $\gamma$ equipped with the uniform norm. We say that the system of monomials $\{z^{p_n}\}_{n\ge 1}$ spans $C(\gamma)$ if the complex linear span of these monomials (restricted to $\gamma$) is dense in $C(\gamma)$.

Question: Does the convergence condition $\sum 1/p_n<\infty$ alone guarantee that the sequence $\{z^{p_n}\}_{n\ge 1}$ fails to span $C(\gamma)$ for every Jordan arc $\gamma$?

(It is known, by results on arcs of locally bounded rotation such as $C^1$ arcs, that the strengthened hypothesis
$$p_n\ge n L(n),\qquad 0<L(n)\uparrow\infty,\qquad \sum\frac{1}{nL(n)}<\infty,$$
already ensures non-spanning; the question asks whether the bare condition $\sum 1/p_n<\infty$ suffices for arbitrary Jordan arcs.)
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returns related work by Korevaar and collaborators (Dixon, Pfluger) on lacunary polynomial approximation and spanning sets of powers on Jordan arcs/curves, including conditions like $p_n\ge nL(n)$ with $\sum 1/(nL(n))<\infty$ that imply non-spanning on arcs of locally bounded rotation. No source found that establishes the bare $\sum 1/p_n<\infty$ condition as sufficient for non-spanning on every Jordan arc, nor a counterexample. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Lacunary Polynomial Approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Korevaar and collaborators studied nonspanning sets of powers on Jordan arcs and curves, with Müntz-type conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist for arcs of locally bounded rotation but the general Jordan arc case under only $\sum 1/p_n<\infty$ is not reported as settled.
